label: D1 after a rewarded rare transition from a1 (a1 -> S2 rare, rewarded)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2) and only when the reward input is 1. 87% of activation mass falls on D1 steps whose previous trial was a1 followed by a rare transition to S2 that was rewarded, which is exactly the rare-rewarded case where a model-based agent should switch. It almost never fires after a2-rare-rewarded (prev_action 2 holds 3.6% of mass) or after common-rewarded trials. Most missed activations are on the window first trial (rel -3), where the previous trial is outside the window, so the predicate cannot see it. The rest are weak activations after common-rewarded trials. Precision is only ~0.52: about half of the a1-rare-rewarded D1 steps stay inactive, and none of the things I tested separate them: the upcoming choice, the policy logit, the good state, value, the trial two back, or episode position. So the feature is a sparse, partial detector of the a1-rare-rewarded history. Uses only observed variables.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & before=a1 S2 u (+2.52), phase=D1 & before=a1 S1 u (+2.33), phase=D1 & last=a1 S2 r (+2.10), last=a1 S2 r (+1.88), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 6 (9 = most a1) (+1.83), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 7 (9 = most a1) (+1.79). Lower it: in_rew=0 (-7.11), prev_state=1 (-5.61), stay=0 (-4.71), action=1 (-3.50).
